startup.name: s2.dev
startup.one_liner: API for unlimited, durable, real-time streams
startup.description: S2 is a serverless API for durable streams that treats streams like object storage, with unlimited streams, access control and direct internet access, aimed at AI agents, real time feeds, sandboxes and local first apps. Usage based pricing for developers and infrastructure teams.

yc_acceptance.basis: YC publishes no acceptance rate; the working prior is about 1 percent with a band of 0.6 to 2 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). This company is already in the batch named in the input, so the number is for completeness only. Five person technical team on a hard infrastructure primitive with a clear thesis; infrastructure and developer tools are well liked by YC but the market for streams is crowded by Kafka vendors; about 1.5 percent. Already in the batch.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: A new database primitive is a slow sell with open source competitors and Kafka compatible vendors, and YC could ask why developers would leave Kafka or managed streaming services and who pays first beyond hobby projects.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Data infrastructure startups often end by acquisition for the team, as Arroyo, Jitsu and Triplit did, or shut down if adoption stays hobbyist. A large exit needs becoming a default building block, as the object storage analogy suggests.

killers.mitigation: Win a use case Kafka serves poorly, such as agent state and per user streams

killers.risk: Hyperscalers or Cloudflare ship an equivalent
killers.evidence: Object storage backed streams are a visible direction for large vendors
killers.mitigation: Open source the core and move faster

killers.risk: Slow usage revenue delays a seed
killers.evidence: Infrastructure revenue follows adoption over many months
killers.mitigation: Charge early and show usage growth

competition_now.name: Confluent and WarpStream
competition_now.what: Kafka and diskless Kafka on object storage

technical_complexity.rationale: Durable distributed logs with strong ordering, unlimited streams and low latency on object storage are hard; a small expert team can build a core in months but operating it reliably at scale is a long, risky effort.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large vendors have distribution and could add a serverless stream primitive; the Kafka diskless proposals show the industry moving in this direction, though a new API gives a differentiated model.

evidence.claim: Vendors are rebuilding streaming on object storage, showing demand for cheaper durable streams
Kafka alternatives are a recognised buying category with paid products

brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "s2.dev" --era 2022+ : invented or proper, name collides with S2 Studio style letter digit names
weaknesses: Hard to search and speak, letter digit name is easily confused
brand.rationale: s2.dev is a short letter plus digit name like S3 that signals the object storage analogy to engineers, but is hard to search and say aloud, so effect is neutral for a developer product.

narrative.headline: A technically deep streaming primitive with a normal seed chance in 13 months and heavy incumbent pull.
narrative.general_summary: s2.dev builds serverless durable streams, positioned as S3 for streams. With a five person technical team and a 13.4 month window, the developer tools cohort gives about 51 percent ever and about 32 percent for the window. Infrastructure investors may back technical credibility early, but analogs show mixed results and no verified rounds for some, so there is no lift above the anchor. The odds do not rank it against others in the batch.
